title: Log-squared sharp threshold for monotone graph properties
exact_target: Does one absolute C bound $p_{1-\epsilon }-p_\epsilon $ by C log(1/(2 epsilon))/(log $n)^2$ for every nonempty proper increasing vertex-relabeling-invariant graph property on $n>=2$ vertices and every epsilon in (0,1/2)?
definition_tex:
\subsection{Definitions and mathematical statement}
\paragraph{Statement recorded in the supplied source.}
Does one absolute C bound $p_{1-\epsilon }-p_\epsilon $ by C log(1/(2 epsilon))/(log $n)^2$ for every nonempty proper increasing vertex-relabeling-invariant graph property on $n>=2$ vertices and every epsilon in (0,1/2)?

\subsection{Short English statement}
Does one absolute C bound $p_{1-\epsilon }-p_\epsilon $ by C log(1/(2 epsilon))/(log $n)^2$ for every nonempty proper increasing vertex-relabeling-invariant graph property on $n>=2$ vertices and every epsilon in (0,1/2)?
